unsupported_claims: Updates only on observed edges, so cost and memory grow with the number of edges rather than the square of the number of nodes, avoiding a dense n×n matrix
The optimization can be parallelized or distributed across machines
It is typically applied to unweighted graphs (the evidence lists Wikipedia, a weighted network, as a dataset, so this is not supported)
Cites Ahmed et al., 2013 (the evidence only gives the reference [1])
rationale: The core claims are supported: SGD optimization makes it scalable, and it applies only to undirected graphs. The answer adds details the evidence does not contain, namely edge-only complexity, distributed optimization, and the restriction to unweighted graphs, and the last of these is arguably contradicted.
